Subject: [PATCH] net: hns3: fix double free bug when setting ringparam

The system will panic when change the ringparam in HNS3 drivers:

Since ndo_stop will reclaim the RX's skb allocated by the driver,
so the backed up ring parameter should not keep this info.

Fixes: a723fb8efe29 ("net: hns3: refine for set ring parameters")
Signed-off-by: Huazhong Tan <tanhuazhong@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
---
 drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c | 4 +++-
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c
index c52eccc1621d..aa692b13b6f3 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c
@@ -908,9 +908,11 @@ static struct hns3_enet_ring *hns3_backup_ringparam(struct hns3_nic_priv *priv)
 	if (!tmp_rings)
 		return NULL;
 
-	for (i = 0; i < handle->kinfo.num_tqps * 2; i++)
+	for (i = 0; i < handle->kinfo.num_tqps * 2; i++) {
 		memcpy(&tmp_rings[i], priv->ring_data[i].ring,
 		       sizeof(struct hns3_enet_ring));
+		tmp_rings[i].skb = NULL;
+	}
 
 	return tmp_rings;
 }
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a double free of memory when changing the ring parameters in the HNS3 driver. Specifically, the driver was not properly managing the state of the `skb` (socket buffer) associated with the rings. When the `ndo_stop` function was called, it reclaimed the RX `skb` allocated by the driver, but the backup ring parameters still retained references to these `skb` objects. This led to a situation where the same memory was attempted to be freed multiple times, resulting in a system panic due to bad page state. The fix involved ensuring that the `skb` pointers in the backed-up ring parameters were set to `NULL` to prevent this double free scenario.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a double free of memory when changing the ring parameters in the HNS3 driver. Specifically, the driver was not properly managing the state of the `skb` (socket buffer) associated with the rings. When the `ndo_stop` function was called, it reclaimed the RX `skb` allocated by the driver, but the backup ring parameters still retained references to these `skb` objects. This led to a situation where the same memory was attempted to be freed multiple times, resulting in a system panic due to bad page state. The fix involved ensuring that the `skb` pointers in the backed-up ring parameters were set to `NULL` to prevent this double free scenario.
